A cloud of anxiety has loomed over the Saudi Arabia national football team’s training camp in Austin, after center-back Hassan Tambakti sustained a muscle injury that forced him out of full team training, just days before the Green Falcons kick off their 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign.

Reports indicate that Tambakti underwent comprehensive medical examinations in Austin on Thursday to determine the exact extent of the damage and his projected spell on the sidelines. The defender felt discomfort in his hamstring during Thursday’s early morning session, prompting the medical and technical staff to immediately withdraw him as a precautionary measure.

#### Donis Prepares Kadesh for Puerto Rico Clash

According to the Saudi newspaper Arriyadiyah, Greek manager Georgios Donis i s leaning heavily toward starting Hassan Kadesh in the lineup for Friday’s friendly against Puerto Rico to fill the void left by Tambakti.

The tactical adjustment underlines the coaching staff’s commitment to maintaining squad readiness while avoiding any further complications that could jeopardize Tambakti’s participation in the upcoming official tournament fixtures.

#### Key Warm-Up Friendlies Ahead of the 2026 World Cup

Saudi Arabia will contest their first friendly against Puerto Rico at the Q2 Stadium in Austin. The team will then travel to face Senegal on June 10 at San Antonio FC‘s stadium, marking the final phase of their preparatory program for the 2026 World Cup.

#### Intensive Training in Austin

On the pitch, the Saudi national team continued their rigorous preparations at the Austin FC training facility. The session began with warm-up drills, moved into ball-possession and finishing exercises, and concluded with a comprehensive, full-pitch tactical scrimmage.

While the session was marred by Tambakti’s premature exit due to injury, goalkeeper Nawaf Al-Aqidi continued his specialized rehabilitation program under medical supervision.

The Green Falcons are scheduled to open their evening training session on Friday (Saudi Arabia time) to the media for the first 15 minutes.

highlights:
## Donis trims Saudi Arabia’s World Cup squad, but debate over omissions continues
[...]
- Left-back Zakaria Hawsawi and attacking midfielder Saleh Abu Al-Shamat omitted from final squad
- They are joined by goalkeeper Abdulqudous Attiah and forward Abdullah Al-Salem
[...]
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s 26-man squad has finally been confirmed ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, but head coach Georgios Donis’ choices have done little to ease concerns among fans ahead of a tough group featuring former world champions Spain and Uruguay.
[...]
With four goalkeepers selected, it was expected that one would not continue to the World Cup. Sure enough, Abdulqudous Attiah dropped out.
[...]
As for Hawsawi and Abu Al-Shamat, the story was different. Reports have emerged that the reason for their inability to make the 26-man squad was lack of fitness.
[...]
Abu Al-Shamat burst onto the scene with Al-Ahli this year but was criticized on multiple occasions due to his inability to consistently complete 90 minutes. In two full Saudi Pro League seasons, the attacking midfielder has yet to feature for a full match.
[...]
But Hawsawi’s absence sparked greater uproar. The Green Falcons’ only natural left-back performed at high levels for Al-Ahli this season, particularly during their run to AFC Champions League Elite glory.
[...]
Regardless, the time for discussion on squad choices is now over. Saudi Arabia have two more friendlies to look forward to following a 2-1 defeat to Ecuador on Sunday, with a match against Puerto Rico on Saturday followed by a meeting with Senegal next Wednesday.

results.title: Saudi Arabia Announces Final Squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup - The Saudi Times
highlights:
Saudi Arabia head coach Georgios Donis has officially announced the Kingdom’s final 26-man squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, as the Green Falcons prepare to compete on football’s biggest stage.
[...]
The squad selection follows months of preparation and evaluation, with the coaching staff choosing the players deemed best equipped to represent Saudi Arabia in the global tournament.
[...]
The goalkeeping department includes Mohammed Al-Owais, Nawaf Al-Aqidi, and Ahmed Al-Kassar.
[...]
In defense, Donis selected Abdulilah Al-Amri, Hassan Tambakti, Jihad Thakri, Ali Lajami, Hassan Kadesh, Saud Abdulhamid, Mohammed Abu Al-Shamat, Ali Majrashi, Moteb Al-Harbi, and Nawaf Boushal.
[...]
The midfield unit features Mohammed Kanno, Abdullah Al-Khaibari, Ziyad Al-Jehani, Nasser Al-Dawsari, Musab Al-Juwayr, Alaa Al-Haji, and team captain Salem Al-Dawsari.
[...]
Leading the attack are Khalid Al-Ghannam, Ayman Yahya, Sultan Mandash, Firas Al-Buraikan, Saleh Al-Shehri, and Abdullah Al-Hamdan.
[...]
## Additional Players Remain on Standby
[...]
The Saudi Football Federation also confirmed that Abdullah Al-Salem, Abdulrahman Al-Sanbi, and Abdulquddus Atiyah will continue training with the national team camp.
[...]
This arrangement is permitted under FIFA regulations, which allow teams to replace injured players up to 24 hours before their opening match. Goalkeepers can also be replaced during the tournament if necessary due to injury.
